name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Lifecycle: /spec:genesis (greenfield) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → /spec:run (design when due, then build, then review, each driver-stepped with one fresh-context reviewer and a derived verdict) → /spec:release; plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.147.0 — spec-review-driver.js refuses a --mark against a spec copy that carries no review sidecar instead of answering it with the terminal cold-path DONE. A mark issued from the main root after a worktree merge landed (status already done, sidecar still in the worktree) exited 0 without dispatching the mark, so finishMerge() never ran: evidence was never promoted and the worktree was never cleaned up, stranding the build and review ledger rows inside a worktree that was then deleted. The refusal names the linked-worktree copy of the spec that owns the sidecar and prints the corrected re-run command; bare and --state invocations still answer DONE. 7.146.0 — Acceptance criteria now declare a mandatory disposition against the test suite they inherit — writes a new test, rewrites a named existing one, or reuses one that already covers the behaviour — written as the AC bullet's trailing arrow pointer with `::` separating the file from a title prefix. ac-matrix --lint refuses a criterion that declares nothing, and --resolve-root refuses a reference that resolves to other than exactly one pre-image test. count-tests.js --root <dir> --titles is where an author finds a reference string. Where a host declares the optional testNameFilter key, red-check verifies each declaration against the NAMED test rather than its whole file: a rewrite must be red against the pre-image and a reuse must be green, so a gutted rewrite and a widened reuse are both caught. A title reaches the runner single-quoted, never interpolated. A filter that selects nothing is invisible to a runner's exit code, so the run's own output naming the title is the only proof of selection — unresolved or unselected falls back to the file's colour with a warning, never a finding. Hosts that declare no testNameFilter keep today's per-file classification exactly. 7.145.0 — The test-case scanner no longer misreads a regex literal as division after an operator or an expression keyword. `lib/scan-test-calls.js` now opens a regex context after `+ - * % < > ~ ^` and after `typeof case await throw else in of` (alongside the existing punctuation, `return` and the `=>` arrow), while a postfix `++`/`--`, a `]`, a grouping paren and a call paren still read the next `/` as division. Before this, a regex holding a quote in one of those positions opened a string span that ran to end of file, swallowing every later line-start test()/it() call and pushing the preceding call's end to src.length. The count was merely wrong; the span is not — specs/20260911/03 deletes expired tests by that span, so an end at EOF would corrupt the file. Eight failing shapes and four division controls are pinned behaviourally, and the live repo's count is unchanged across all of its test files.
